## [0.17.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.16.0...v0.17.0) (2026-11-14)
Finishing touches to the column layout.
### Features
* **A Folders button on the Windows toolbar** shows and hides the folder list, and stays pressed while the list is shown, like the sidebar buttons on the Mac and Linux. * **The sorted column shows its arrow** in the Windows message list's headings, pointing up or down with the order. * **Watched and ignored conversations are marked** in the column layout's rows on Linux, as they are on Windows and the Mac. * The Windows main window keeps a size its toolbar and panes fit in. * The help for Options describes Layout and the pictures in the list.

## [0.16.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.15.0...v0.16.0) (2026-11-13)
A column layout for wide screens, on Windows, the Mac and Linux.
### Features
* **The column layout.** On a wide screen the folders, the messages and the message you read sit side by side, and each message is a row of three lines: who sent it and when, the subject, and the first words of the message, without the earlier messages it quotes. View > Layout chooses Automatic (the default: the column layout in a window 1320 wide or wider, the classic one below 1200), Classic or Columns; the same choice is in Options (Settings on the Mac, Preferences on Linux). The classic layout is unchanged. * **Senders' pictures** in the column layout: a brand's logo when your mail provider verified it, the picture of a contact for mail your provider confirmed comes from them, and quiet initials for everyone else. A logo is downloaded once for each brand, never for each message. * **A picture for each contact.** Contact Properties takes a PNG or JPEG picture, chosen or dropped on it; vCard files carry it in and out. A forged message from a contact's address shows initials, never the picture. * **Hide the folder list** with View > Folder List (F9, Control-Command-S on the Mac), the close box on its Folders caption on Windows, or the sidebar button on the Mac and Linux. On Windows the folder bar then drops the list down. * **View > Sort By** sorts by date, sender, subject or size, ascending or descending, in both layouts. * Plain text messages keep lines of a readable length in a wide reading pane. * Windows remembers the window's place and the sizes of its panes.
### Bug Fixes
* A conversation's row shows the first words of the message that opens when you select it.

## [0.15.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.14.2...v0.15.0) (2026-11-13)
Messages open faster, on Windows, the Mac and Linux.
### Features
* **New mail is downloaded as it arrives**, so it opens at once, also offline. Settings (Options on Windows, Preferences on Linux) has a new Downloading section: download recent messages up to 1 MB ahead (the default), all messages, or only when opened, and how much each account keeps (1 GB to begin with; past it the oldest go, and download again when opened). Junk E-mail, Deleted Items and Gmail's All Mail are downloaded only when opened. * **The messages above and below the one opened are fetched too**, for Next and Previous. * **A large message shows its text first.** Over 1 MB, its text and pictures show before its attachments; the status bar says how far the rest is. * **The downloading page says how large the message is.** * A new app icon.
### Performance Improvements
* The connection that downloads opened messages is ready before the first click and kept alive; one that went dead (after sleep, a network change, or a router that forgot it) is replaced within seconds instead of after five minutes. * Indexing for search and threading runs on a connection of its own, so new mail no longer waits behind it. * A click during a large download is answered at once, and drafts and the copies of sent messages are uploaded without holding up anything else. * A server that allows only one connection still gets all of this done on that one.
### Bug Fixes
* A one-time code in a new mail notification no longer leaves an IMAP response half read. * A message the server refuses to give text for no longer holds up the search index of the rest. * A moved or archived message keeps its downloaded copy. * The small app icon's corners stay clear at 16 pixels.
